member: a slab-heated (TABS) office, 150 m^2, brine-to-water heat pump on a Spanish 2.0TD tariff, medium-mass envelope; the task represents the family of slab-heated offices (hvac/PHYSICS.md:5-7)

cop_carnot_fraction.why: ours, family range 0.50 to 0.57 from brine heat pump datasheets [18]; hvac/PHYSICS.md:61, env.py:96-101

T_brine.why: ours, family range -5 to 5 C for a ground loop in the heating season; hvac/PHYSICS.md:62, env.py:102-104

occupants_per_m2.why: ours, family range 0.07 to 0.12 (8 to 15 m^2 a person); hvac/PHYSICS.md:65, env.py:159-160

comfort_price.why: DERIVED, not a stated range: comfort_price = productivity_per_K x occupants x 150 m^2 x labour_cost (hvac/PHYSICS.md:71, env.py:164-166) at occupants 0.07 and 0.12, i.e. 0.02*0.07*150*31.8 and 0.02*0.12*150*31.8

concrete_heat_capacity.why: ours (ISO 10456 as commonly quoted, not read); published range 0.8 to 1.2 kJ/(kg K), converted to J; hvac/PHYSICS.md:57

concrete_conductivity.why: ours (ISO 10456 as commonly quoted, not read); published range 1.5 to 3.5 W/(m K); hvac/PHYSICS.md:57

coupled_why: comfort_price is the work an occupied kelvin-hour loses and is defined as productivity_per_K x occupants x 150 m^2 x labour_cost (hvac/PHYSICS.md:71), so it moves with the occupant density: the low end 0.07 goes with 6.678 and 0.12 with 11.448
